clinician.trajectory_summary: A 44-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of pruritic rash involving the extremities, oral cavity, groin, abdomen, axillae, and gluteal region. On admission, clinical examination revealed well-demarcated erythematous plaques with tiny fragile vesicles at the margins. Laboratory workup showed hyperglycemia (132 mg/dL), elevated chromogranin A (243 ng/mL), newly diagnosed diabetes mellitus, and anemia (Hb 11.4 g/dL). Skin biopsy demonstrated histopathologic findings consistent with necrolytic migratory erythema (NME), including psoriasiform acanthosis, abrupt necrosis of the upper stratum, perivascular lymphocytic infiltration, and extravasated red blood cells. Serum glucagon was markedly elevated at 720 ng/L (normal 40-130 ng/L). Contrast-enhanced CT imaging revealed a 3-cm enhancing mass in the pancreatic head. Pathology from the pancreatic mass confirmed neuroendocrine carcinoma with evidence of vascular and perineural invasion, establishing the diagnosis of glucagonoma.
